name: Seltorexant
summary: Seltorexant (JNJ-42847922, MIN-202) is J&J's oral, once-daily selective orexin-2 receptor antagonist, developed as an add-on to an SSRI or SNRI in adults with major depressive disorder with insomnia symptoms who responded inadequately to the antidepressant. The Phase 3 record is mixed: MDD3001 (NCT04533529) met all primary and secondary endpoints (J&J, 2024-05-29), MDD3002 (NCT04532749) was stopped at an interim analysis on the data monitoring committee's advice, and MDD3005 (NCT04513912) missed its primary endpoint against quetiapine XR (response 57.4% vs 53.4% at 26 weeks, J&J, 2025-09-22). The filing now rests on NCT06559306 (adjunctive, 752 participants, primary completion 2026-12-30), with a monotherapy Phase 3, NCT07573176 (600 participants, 2028-08), behind it. Price anchor: Caplyta, J&J's own adjunctive-MDD brand, at $9,940 per CMS Part D beneficiary in 2024. Uptake anchor: Auvelity's measured Medicare capture of 0.1417% a year and its launch curve, the book's MDD seed values (brenipatide). J&J pays a mid-single-digit royalty on worldwide sales, now held by Royalty Pharma.

therapy_mode.source: NCT06559306 (book trials table): daily adjunctive seltorexant added to an ongoing SSRI/SNRI, MADRS change at Day 43; MDD3001 (NCT04533529) carried a long-term safety extension, and NCT03321526 dosed for 24 weeks (Pinter et al., Int J Neuropsychopharmacol 2026;29(4), doi:10.1093/ijnp/pyag009, PMID 41795948)
therapy_mode.note: An add-on taken daily with the patient's antidepressant for as long as the episode and its maintenance last, so chronic by the house definition
therapy_mode.check: Book trials table: NCT06559306 is adjunctive seltorexant added to an ongoing SSRI/SNRI, primary MADRS change at Day 43. Trial listings surfaced by search (J&J clinicaltrials.jnj.com, UChicago, CenterWatch) describe it as a two-part placebo-controlled Phase 3 of 20 mg seltorexant: Part 2 measures time to relapse in a double-blind maintenance phase after a stable response on open-label seltorexant. A maintenance design means continuous daily dosing. Book completed_trials: NCT04533529 (MDD3001) title includes a long-term safety extension. PubMed 41795948 (Pinter et al., IJNP 2026;29(4), doi:10.1093/ijnp/pyag009): once-daily dosing over a 24-week double-blind phase in NCT03321526. Chronic holds

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Caplyta: CMS Medicare Part D 2024, $268,479,293.41 over 27,010 beneficiaries = $9,940 per beneficiary
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement on the comparator. Seltorexant's setting is the adjunctive-MDD slot that atypical antipsychotics hold, and J&J ran it head to head against quetiapine XR in that slot (NCT04513912, NCT03321526). Caplyta is J&J's own brand in that slot, with an adjunctive-MDD label from 6 November 2025 (J&J release; the date was checked by the second reader of the LLY brenipatide seed). Cross-check: Vraylar, the book's anchor for brenipatide in the same disease, reads $9,662 (lookup.py demand Vraylar, Part D 2024), 3% lower. The case against: Caplyta's 2024 Medicare spend is schizophrenia and bipolar depression use, before its MDD label. Per-beneficiary spend covers part of a year, so it understates an annual price. The orexin class sells for far less: Belsomra reads $1,948 per beneficiary (Part D 2024), and Auvelity, the newest MDD-only brand, $4,686. Payers may also put generic quetiapine and aripiprazole first. No list price for seltorexant has been published, since it is not approved
list_price_per_patient.check: lookup.py demand Caplyta: Part D 2024 $268,479,293.41 / 27,010 beneficiaries = $9,940.00, so 0.00994 mm USD per patient-year is right in unit. Caplyta's MDD approval is listed in J&J's Q4 2025 earnings exhibit (8-K 0000200406-26-000002, book filing_sections: 'approvals of CAPLYTA for major depressive disorder'). The 6 November 2025 date comes from the brenipatide second reader; I did not re-check it. Cross-checks recomputed from lookup.py demand, Part D 2024: Vraylar $9,662, Belsomra $1,948, Auvelity $4,686. The head-to-head trials against quetiapine XR are confirmed: MDD3005 (J&J release; also listed in the Q3 2025 8-K 0000200406-25-000201) and NCT03321526 (PubMed 41795948). The comparator choice is a labelled judgement with its case against (orexin class and newest MDD brand priced lower; pre-MDD-label spend)

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention on a CMS Part D per-beneficiary price (backend/gross_to_net.py: halving lands at a median 96% of CMS's own negotiated net prices); the Caplyta anchor is Part D (lookup.py demand Caplyta, part D)
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: 0.5 is the share taken off list, so net is $4,970 per patient-year
gross_to_net_pct.check: Anchor is Part D (lookup.py demand Caplyta, part D), so the house convention of 0.5 applies. The direction is right: 0.5 is the share taken off list, so net is 0.5 x $9,940 = $4,970 per patient-year

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: NCT03321526, seltorexant vs quetiapine XR as add-on to an SSRI/SNRI, 24-week double-blind phase: all-cause study-drug discontinuation 41.2% on seltorexant vs 47.1% on quetiapine XR (Pinter et al., Int J Neuropsychopharmacol 2026;29(4), doi:10.1093/ijnp/pyag009, PMID 41795948)
discontinuation_pct.note: Constant hazard: 1 - (1 - 0.412)^(365.25/168) = 0.685 a year. This is the asset's own measured stop rate, in the label's setting. It replaces the book's other MDD value (brenipatide, 0.648), which comes from GLP-1 use in obesity. The case for lower: the study was exploratory and flexibly dosed at 20 or 40 mg, the 40 mg dose did not work, and stops for lack of efficacy may fall at the 20 mg label dose. The case for higher: trial retention usually beats real-world persistence on antidepressants and add-ons
discontinuation_pct.check: PubMed 41795948 abstract (Pinter et al., NCT03321526, 24-week double-blind phase): all-cause study drug discontinuation 41.2% on seltorexant vs 47.1% on quetiapine-XR (2-sided P = .5355). Hazard ratio 0.83 (80% CI 0.6-1.2). Efficacy was seen at 20 mg but not 40 mg. Recomputed: 1 - (1 - 0.412)^(365.25/168) = 0.6848. The study is small (107 enrolled, book completed_trials) and exploratory, and was flexibly dosed at 20 or 40 mg, as the note says. Using the asset's own measured rate is a labelled judgement with the case both ways

forecast_start_year.source: NCT06559306 primary completion 2026-12-30, estimated (context file and book trials table); NCT07573176 primary completion 2028-08-24
forecast_start_year.note: Judgement on the timeline. MDD3001 is one positive placebo-controlled study. MDD3002 was stopped at interim and MDD3005 missed against quetiapine XR, so the filing waits on NCT06559306. On a readout in early 2027, J&J files in 2027 and a standard 12-month review for a new molecular entity puts US approval in 2028, so 2029 is the first full year. The case against: if NCT06559306 fails, the monotherapy study (primary completion 2028-08) is the next chance, which pushes launch to 2030 or 2031. No J&J filing date was found in search
forecast_start_year.check: A filing path remains, so the asset is not refused. (1) MDD3001 (NCT04533529) met all primary and secondary endpoints: J&J release of 29 May 2024, via search. (2) MDD3002 (NCT04532749) was stopped after an interim analysis on the Independent Data Monitoring Committee's recommendation. The SAP makes that interim a futility look. Actual primary completion 24 May 2022, results posted 4 June 2025 (ClinicalTrials.gov record and SAP, via search). (3) MDD3005 (NCT04513912): response at 26 weeks 57.4% vs 53.4% on quetiapine XR, difference 4.0% (95% CI -3.3 to 11.3), not significant (J&J release 'numerically higher response', via search). That was an active-comparator superiority test, not a failed placebo-controlled study. (4) NCT06559306 is a second placebo-controlled adjunctive Phase 3 of the 20 mg dose (via search). Book: 752 participants, estimated primary completion 2026-12-30, unchanged since the 2026-07-18 snapshot, still recruiting at last update 2026-08-28. With MDD3001 it would give the two positive placebo-controlled studies a US NDA normally needs. (5) J&J is still investing: the monotherapy Phase 3 NCT07573176 started 2026-04-30, and Phase 3 data went to the 2026 Psych Congress (search). No US submission is announced: seltorexant is absent from J&J's Q4 2025, Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 earnings exhibits in the book's filing_sections. On that record, a 2027 readout and filing, a 2028 approval and 2029 as the first full year is a reasonable labelled judgement. Risk to add: the study was still recruiting four months before its estimated primary completion, so the readout could slip into mid-2027 and push 2029 to 2030

exus_multiple.source: Spravato FY2025: $210mm international against $1,485mm US (J&J FY2025 10-K 0000200406-26-000016, in the book's asset_revenue_regions for esketamine, sec_fsds)
exus_multiple.note: Judgement on the comparator. Spravato is J&J's own depression brand with a filed geographic split. Caplyta, its adjunctive-MDD brand, books nothing outside the US (book: FY2025 NonUs $0 against US $700mm). The case for higher: an oral pill is easier to launch ex-US than an in-clinic nasal spray under a REMS, and seltorexant's Phase 3 programme enrolled globally. The case for lower: ex-US payers price adjunctive antidepressants low
exus_multiple.check: Book asset_revenue_regions (esketamine, FY2025, sec_fsds, 10-K 0000200406-26-000016): US $1,485mm, NonUs $210mm; 210 / 1,485 = 0.1414. The same split is in J&J's Q4 2025 earnings exhibit (8-K 0000200406-26-000002): SPRAVATO twelve months US 1,485, Intl 210, WW 1,696. H1 2026 cross-check: US 920, Intl 131 = 0.142 (8-K 0000200406-26-000146). Caplyta FY2025 US $700mm, NonUs $0 confirmed. The comparator choice is a labelled judgement

economics_share.source: Minerva Neurosciences FY2020 10-K (sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1598646/000156459021011340): Minerva opted out of the Janssen agreement on 30 June 2020 under a settlement of 24 June 2020 and is 'entitled to collect a royalty on worldwide sales of seltorexant in certain indications in the mid-single digits'. Opt-out 8-K exhibit: sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1598646/000119312520185290/d947910dex991.htm. Royalty Pharma bought the royalty on 19 January 2021 for $60mm upfront and up to $95mm in milestones, which Royalty Pharma pays, not J&J (Royalty Pharma and Minerva releases). House convention: a royalty is netted at the lowest stated tier over the company's pre-tax margin. The Ralinepag seed nets 'at the lowest tier ... as every royalty in the book is'. The Litifilimab seed takes a mid-single-digit Royalty Pharma royalty 'at the bottom of that range', 4%. The disitamab vedotin and vepdegestrant seeds also use the lowest tier. J&J cost rows (lookup.py seed Esketamine Hydrochloride): cogs 0.259683, sga 0.198379, rd 0.195808, other_costs -0.044065, so margin = 0.390195
economics_share.note: A royalty J&J PAYS, netted as (margin - royalty) / margin = (0.390195 - 0.04) / 0.390195 = 0.8975. It uses 4%, the bottom of 'mid-single digits', which is the book's convention for every royalty. Corrected by the second reader from 0.8719, which took 5%, the middle of the range. At 5% the share is 0.8719, and at 6% it is 0.8462. No filing gives the exact rate. The case against: 'certain indications' leaves open whether a monotherapy label (NCT07573176) pays the royalty. The adjunctive MDD use modelled here was inside the original co-development scope, so it should pay it
economics_share.check: 0.8719 -> 0.8975. The terms are confirmed by search: Minerva's FY2020 10-K wording ('royalty on worldwide sales of seltorexant in certain indications in the mid-single digits', opt-out 30 June 2020), and Royalty Pharma's purchase of the royalty on 19 January 2021 for $60mm upfront plus up to $95mm in milestones. I did not see the June 2020 8-K's 'all indications' wording. Margin recomputed: 1 - 0.259683 - 0.198379 - 0.195808 + 0.044065 = 0.390195. The researcher's arithmetic at 5% holds (0.8719), but the rate breaks the book's convention of netting every royalty at the lowest stated tier: the Ralinepag seed says so, and the Litifilimab seed reads 'mid-single-digit' at its bottom, 4%. (0.390195 - 0.04) / 0.390195 = 0.897487

eligible_pct.source: Three filters, applied to the NSDUH past-year MDE pool. (1) Treated: 61.0% of US adults with a past-year MDE received treatment (NIMH, nimh.nih.gov/health/statistics/major-depression, NSDUH 2021), the book's brenipatide value. (2) Inadequate response to an SSRI: 47% responded (50% or more QIDS-SR reduction) to citalopram in STAR*D level 1 among 2,876 US outpatients, so 53% did not (Trivedi et al., Am J Psychiatry 2006;163:28-40, doi:10.1176/appi.ajp.163.1.28, PMID 16390886). (3) Insomnia symptoms: 'approximately 60 percent of MDD patients on standard-of-care oral antidepressants experience residual insomnia symptoms' (J&J MDD3001 release, 2024-05-29, jnj.com/media-center/press-releases/johnson-johnson-pivotal-study-of-seltorexant-shows-statistically-significant-and-clinically-meaningful-improvement-in-depressive-symptoms-and-sleep-disturbance-outcomes). 0.61 x 0.53 x 0.60 = 0.19398
eligible_pct.note: Judgement: the filters are taken as independent. The label population follows the Phase 3 entry criteria: MDD with insomnia symptoms and an inadequate response to an ongoing SSRI/SNRI (NCT04533529 and NCT06559306 titles; NCT03321526 enrolled inadequate response to 1-3 SSRIs/SNRIs). The case for higher: insomnia is more common in non-responders than the 60% across all treated patients. STAR*D found some insomnia symptom in 84.7% of 3,743 outpatients at baseline, of any severity (Sunderajan et al., CNS Spectr 2010;15(6):394-404, doi:10.1017/s1092852900029266, PMID 20625372). A monotherapy label (NCT07573176) would also drop filter (2). The case for lower: the 60% is J&J's own figure, not a paper, and the trials require moderate-to-severe insomnia. 'Treated' also includes talk therapy alone, while the label needs an ongoing SSRI/SNRI. Filters (2) and (3) cut deeper into the one MDD pool the book carries, so the seltorexant and brenipatide labels overlap only in part
eligible_pct.check: All three inputs confirmed. (1) NIMH/NSDUH 2021, 61.0% treated: the book's brenipatide eligible_pct row, confirmed there by its second reader. (2) Trivedi et al. 2006 (PubMed 16390886, doi:10.1176/appi.ajp.163.1.28): QIDS-SR response 47% among 2,876 analysed STAR*D level-1 citalopram outpatients, so 53% did not respond. (3) J&J MDD3001 release, 29 May 2024, via search: 'Approximately 60% of MDD patients on standard-of-care oral antidepressants experience residual insomnia symptoms'. Recomputed: 0.61 x 0.53 x 0.60 = 0.19398. Sunderajan et al. 2010 (PubMed 20625372): insomnia symptoms in 84.7% of 3,743 STAR*D outpatients, confirmed. The label population matches: NCT06559306 enrols MDD with insomnia symptoms and an inadequate response to a current SSRI/SNRI (search listing). Independence of the filters is a labelled judgement with the case both ways

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the untreated eligible pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: Auvelity, as measured in the book's brenipatide seed (second-reader corrected): 16,448 Part D beneficiaries in 2024 and 9,268 in 2023 (lookup.py demand Auvelity). New patients in 2024 = 16,448 - 9,268 x (1 - 0.648) = 13,186, over a Medicare pool of 53.1mm Part D enrollees (KFF 2024) x 17.54% with depressive disorders (CMS Chronic Conditions Warehouse, 2022) = 9,313,740, less 9,268 = 0.1417%
penetration_peak_pct.note: Judgement: a 1.0x multiple on Auvelity, the newest oral MDD brand with a clean CMS series. It applies the rate Auvelity took of its own label pool (all diagnosed MDD) to seltorexant's narrower label pool. At peak that is 21,414,000 x 0.19398 x 0.001417 = about 5,900 new patients a year. The case for higher: if seltorexant won as many patients as Auvelity in absolute terms, the rate on its narrower pool would be 0.001417 / (0.53 x 0.60) = 0.0045. A label defined by insomnia also gives prescribers a clear patient type, and J&J sells Spravato and Caplyta to the same prescribers. 2024 was also Auvelity's second full year, not its peak. The case for lower: a mixed Phase 3 record, a failed head-to-head against generic quetiapine XR, and near-free generic sleep aids (trazodone, mirtazapine) already used for insomnia in depression. The Auvelity Medicare-diagnosed pool is broader than MDD (it includes dysthymia and other depressive disorders), and the rate is applied to an all-payer US pool
penetration_peak_pct.check: Recomputed: 16,448 - 9,268 x (1 - 0.648) = 13,186 (lookup.py demand Auvelity, 2023 and 2024). The pool is 53.1mm x 17.54% = 9,313,740, less 9,268 = 9,304,472, which gives 0.14171%. This matches the brenipatide seed row exactly (lookup.py seed Brenipatide). KFF and CCW inputs were confirmed by that seed's second reader. The peak arithmetic holds: 21,414,000 x 0.19398 x 0.001417 = 5,886 new patients a year (the note says about 5,900). Sensitivity: the solve uses the brenipatide stop rate (0.648) for Auvelity's stock. With seltorexant's own 0.6848 it gives 13,527 / 9,304,472 = 0.1454%, 2.6% higher. It is kept because Auvelity's own persistence is unsourced and the brief says to reuse measured values. The 1.0x rate on a label pool a third of brenipatide's implies under half of Auvelity's Medicare-only 2024 new starts, all-payer. That is disclosed in the case for higher, so it stays a labelled judgement

ramp_steepness.check: ln(16,448 / 9,268) = ln(1.7747) = 0.5736 (lookup.py demand Auvelity). This matches the brenipatide seed row (0.574)
